topic: Blood transfusion and cross-matching in arthroplasty

audits.title: A one-centre prospective audit of peri- and postoperative blood loss and transfusion practice in patients undergoing hip or knee replacement surgery.

cycle1.result: Blood loss recorded in only 57% of operations; MSBOS compliance variable; blood issued pre-operatively in 86% and 75% of these transfused; 26% of transfusions not recorded in medical or nursing notes.

audits.other_findings: Pre- and postoperative haemoglobin similar in transfused and non-transfused groups, suggesting transfusion by habit rather than indication.
audits.citation: Roberts M, Ahya R, Greaves M, Maffulli N. A one-centre prospective audit of peri- and postoperative blood loss and transfusion practice in patients undergoing hip or knee replacement surgery. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2000;82(1):44-48. PMID: 10700768.

audits.title: An audit on the blood transfusion requirements for revision hip arthroplasty.
audits.standard: Trust maximum surgical blood ordering schedule (MSBOS): 6 units of blood for revision hip arthroplasty
audits.setting: Departments of Orthopaedics and Audit, Princess Margaret Hospital, Swindon

cycle1.result: 80.3% received less than 6 units, 12.2% received 6 units and 7.5% received more than 6 units

audits.other_findings: 14 patients had postoperative Hb < 9 g/dl and needed additional units; authors suggest 4 units rather than 6 when pre-operative Hb is 13 g/dl or more.
audits.citation: Sharma S, Cooper H, Ivory JP. An audit on the blood transfusion requirements for revision hip arthroplasty. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2002;84(4):269-272. doi:10.1308/003588402320439720. PMID: 12215032.

audits.title: Audit on the efficient use of cross-matched blood in elective total hip and total knee replacement.
audits.standard: Maximum Surgical Blood Ordering Schedule (MSBOS) and national guidelines
audits.setting: Orthopaedic unit, Stoke Mandeville Hospital; elective TKR and THR

cycle1.result: High level of unnecessary cross-matched blood; THR cross-match transfusion (C:T) ratio 3.21

audits.intervention: Ceased routine cross-matching for THR; check full blood count on day 2 after surgery for all patients; Hb-based criteria (detail truncated)

cycle2.result: Units cross-matched but not transfused fell by 96% for THR; C:T ratio reduced to 1.62

audits.other_findings: 301 patients in total over the year; reductions also seen for TKR. Telephone survey: 20 of 44 hospitals routinely cross-matched for THR and 11 for TKR.
audits.citation: Rogers BA, Johnstone DJ. Audit on the efficient use of cross-matched blood in elective total hip and total knee replacement. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2006;88(2):199-201. doi:10.1308/003588406x82952. PMID: 16551419.

audits.title: Blood audit evidenced-based cross-match requesting for lumbar spine surgery.
audits.standard: Evidence-based cross-match tariff (cross-match to transfusion ratio and transfusion index)
audits.setting: Spinal surgery department, Derriford Hospital, Plymouth; elective lumbar spine operations excluding deformity

cycle1.result: 664 cross-match requests, 40 units transfused; C:T ratio 16.6:1.

audits.intervention: New evidence-based cross-match tariff agreed between surgeons, anaesthetists and transfusion department.
audits.citation: Clarke A, O'Malley M, Hegarty JF, Freeman BJ. Blood audit evidenced-based cross-match requesting for lumbar spine surgery. Spine (Phila Pa 1976). 2006;31(12):E373-5. doi:10.1097/01.brs.0000219404.64336.9a. PMID: 16721282.

audits.title: National comparative audit of blood use in elective primary unilateral total hip replacement surgery in the UK.
audits.standard: National comparative audit indicators and standards for transfusion practice
audits.setting: 223 UK hospitals, NHS Blood and Transplant national comparative audit

cycle1.result: 47% of hospitals had a transfusion policy; 73% did group-and-save rather than cross-match; of patients transfused, 7% had a single unit and 67% two units; 65% of those given two or more units had post-transfusion Hb 10 g/dl or more.

audits.other_findings: 15% had pre-operative Hb below 12 g/dl, and 57% of these were transfused compared with 20% with higher values; wide variation in transfusion rates between hospitals.
audits.citation: Boralessa H, Goldhill DR, Tucker K, Mortimer AJ, Grant-Casey J. National comparative audit of blood use in elective primary unilateral total hip replacement surgery in the UK. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2009;91(7):599-605. doi:10.1308/003588409x432464. PMID: 19686612.

audits.title: The appropriateness of blood transfusion following primary total hip replacement.
audits.standard: British Orthopaedic Association guidelines on blood conservation in elective orthopaedic surgery

cycle1.result: 39/143 (27%) transfused; 18/39 (46%) inappropriate, 9/39 (23%) appropriate, 5/39 (13%) over-transfused, 7/39 (18%) not assessable.

audits.intervention: Staff education and amendments to local transfusion policy.
audits.other_findings: 52% of patients with drains (29/56) were transfused.
audits.citation: Joy PJ, Bennet SJ. The appropriateness of blood transfusion following primary total hip replacement. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2012;94(3):201-203. doi:10.1308/003588412x13171221501384. PMID: 22507728.

audits.title: Primary elective spine arthrodesis: Audit of institutional cross matched to transfused (C/T) ratio to develop blood product ordering guidelines.
audits.standard: Cross-matched to transfused (C/T) ratio compared with the optimal 2:1 reported in the literature
audits.setting: Department of Neurosurgery, Aga Khan University (single institution), elective spinal arthrodesis

cycle1.result: 292 units of packed red cells cross-matched, 66 transfused (C/T ratio 4.4:1); 39 of 85 patients (45.88%) transfused. C/T 6.9:1 for degenerative disease and 23:1 for cervical spine.

audits.intervention: Recommended a blood ordering schedule: two units for preoperative haemoglobin <9 g/dl, trauma, adult idiopathic scoliosis or more than two levels; group and hold for the rest. Not re-audited.
audits.other_findings: On multivariate analysis only indication for surgery was independently associated with transfusion (AIS adjusted OR 124.87, trauma 34.37 versus degenerative disease).
audits.citation: Alam MM, Sobani ZA, Shamim MS, Ahmad K, Minai F. Primary elective spine arthrodesis: Audit of institutional cross matched to transfused (C/T) ratio to develop blood product ordering guidelines. Surg Neurol Int. 2013;4(Suppl 5):S368-72. doi:10.4103/2152-7806.120778. PMID: 24340234.

audits.title: Perioperative Blood Management, Red Cell Recovery (Cell Salvage) Practice in an Australian Tertiary Hospital: A Hospital District Clinical Audit.
audits.setting: Gold Coast Hospital and Health Service, 2-campus tertiary hospital

cycle1.result: 79% compliance with national guidelines; orthopaedics used most cases (22.9%, n = 108).

audits.other_findings: Highest average return in vascular surgery (699 mL) and urology (654 mL); revision (7.6%) and primary (6.6%) THR among most common procedures.
audits.citation: Forrest EA, Togo P, Kan AG, De Cruz SE. Perioperative Blood Management, Red Cell Recovery (Cell Salvage) Practice in an Australian Tertiary Hospital: A Hospital District Clinical Audit. Anesth Analg. 2019;128(6):1272-1278. doi:10.1213/ane.0000000000003595. PMID: 31094799.

audits.title: Cross-Matching in Spinal Surgery - An Audit of Compliance at the National Spinal Injuries Unit (NSIU).
audits.setting: National Spinal Injuries Unit (NSIU); spinal surgery
audits.intervention: Revised spine-specific departmental transfusion guideline aligned with MSBOS.
audits.other_findings: Unnecessary cross-matching fell without compromising peri-operative safety.

audits.title: A retrospective audit of blood loss in total hip joint replacement surgery at Middlemore Hospital.
audits.standard: Transfusion justified only for 30% red cell volume loss or loss dropping haematocrit below 0.28
audits.setting: Middlemore Hospital, Otahuhu, Auckland; retrospective record review

cycle1.result: Primary hip replacement: 58 of 104 transfused, 157 units, 37 (24%) inappropriate. Complex hip replacement: 32 of 38 transfused, 139 units, 12 (9%) inappropriate.

audits.other_findings: Two-unit transfusion was commonly given when one unit would have sufficed; concurrent audit recommended.
audits.citation: Gillham M, Mark A. A retrospective audit of blood loss in total hip joint replacement surgery at Middlemore Hospital. N Z Med J. 1997;110(1049):294-297. PMID: 9293284.
